proposedOverrides.summary: Atlas-aware Hispaniola history: Taíno survival, African agency, slavery, daily life, partition, and continuity.

batchIdentityNotes: Hispaniola (Spain) is a generated atlas label, not a contemporary sovereign-state name or uniform identity.
The 1530 and 1600 target geometry combines Hispaniola, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico; the 1650 and 1700 geometry combines Hispaniola and Puerto Rico.
Several historically important coastal places fall outside the simplified polygons, so card claims use named sources rather than polygon membership as historical proof.
Spanish authority varied sharply across named towns, ranches, maroon zones, mountains, coasts, and islands.
Taíno demographic catastrophe is never described as disappearance; survivors, descendants, practices, and agency continue throughout and beyond the period.
Ryswick recognized French possession in western Hispaniola in 1697, while the atlas delays its split until 1715 and mislabels sampled Puerto Rico at that seam.
